tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use when the user asks whether...'), focuses on user intent (resilience, failover, traffic loss investigation) with explicit trigger contexts, and remains concise while covering scope and constraints (read-only nature).
tests.evidence: Use when the user asks whether their Direct Connect setup is resilient, whether failover will work, whether the same routes/prefixes are advertised across redundant VIFs, why traffic was lost after a VIF or connection failure, or to audit DX BGP route symmetry.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and focused on domain-specific, non-obvious facts (route-view convergence lag, LAG caveats, CIDR coverage rules, tiered redundancy resolution) rather than explaining general concepts like what BGP or Direct Connect is.
tests.evidence: Route-view convergence lag (critical). ListVirtualInterfaceRoutes returns an eventually-consistent view that lags live BGP...

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only constraints, CIDR math delegation, tiered redundancy resolution, severity interpretation) are given exact prescriptive steps, while flexible parts (report language translation, judgment on partial supernet severity) leave room for agent judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: Never do CIDR coverage math yourself... Your job is orchestration, judgment, and translation into customer language.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill designates clear default tools per step (e.g., analyze_vif_resilience, compare_prefix_sets) without presenting a menu of equal alternative tools.
tests.evidence: Call analyze_vif_resilience(vif_ids, directions=["accepted","advertised"]) once per set.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (discover estate, resolve redundant sets by precedence, analyze, interpret severity, validate, deliver) that applies to any DX VIF resilience assessment, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Work through this checklist in order; each step depends on the one before it. - [ ] Step 1: Discover the estate ...
